chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all together from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
He was asked about the crescents, so he said: 'They are the crescents of the months. So whenever you see the new moon, fast; and when you see it (again), break your fast.'

key_terms.الْأَهِلَّةِ: The plural of hilal (crescent/new moon); used to ask about the purpose and function of the lunar calendar phases
key_terms.فَأَفْطِرْ: Imperative: 'break your fast!' — the legal injunction to end Ramadan upon sighting the new moon of Shawwal
key_terms.فَصُمْ: Imperative: 'fast!' — the legal injunction to begin sawm (fasting) upon sighting the new moon
key_terms.هِلَال: Hilal — the crescent moon at the beginning of the lunar month, used to mark the start of Ramadan and Eid

ai.seo_question: When should fasting begin and end in Islam according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) was asked about the significance of the crescent moons (ahilla) and responded with a Quranically-grounded ruling: the new moon sighting determines the beginning and end of the month of Ramadan. The question aligns with Quran 2:189, where the Prophet was asked about the crescent moons. For the early Muslim community, this hadith clarified that the visual sighting of the crescent — not astronomical calculation — is the jurisprudential basis for beginning and ending the fast.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, altogether from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad Bin Usman, from Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘He<sup>asws</sup>
was asked about the crescent, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is the crescent of the month. So whenever you see the new moon, so Fast, and when you see it (again), so break the Fasting’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father and Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad all from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad ibn ‘Uthman from al-Halabiy who has said the following: “Abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,

was asked about the crescents (mentioned in the holy Quran). He (the Imam) replied, ‘It is a reference to the new moon of the months. When you see the new moon, begin fasting; when you see the new moon discontinue fasting.’”
